56699-the-stone-axe-of-burkamukk:
Mary Grant Bruce, the Australian writer for the young, published this set of Aboriginal tales in 1922, illustrated by J Macfarlane. The title story gives the book its name. Other tales tell of Waung the crow, the emu who would dance, and Booran the pelican.

Burkamukk the chief chose his camp in a green glade by a wide creek, near a swamp full of food. His people were fat and content, with plenty of skin rugs sewn with sinew and kangaroo bone needles. The contents run on through the story of the stars, how light came, and the frog that laughed. Wurip the fire-bringer closes the set. Bruce retells the dreamtime tales in her own warm prose.

The guest, now cast out from the firm he helped build, names a top villain in political media. Talk turns raw on race, fame, and old grudges. Jones lets the guest vent while testing his claims. The episode captures a media insider in exile, bitter and blunt, with a story that mainstream outlets rarely air in full.
